title: Course Group By Field
prompt: A course dashboard needs to group course lessons by a chosen field. Write a function that returns an object where each field value maps to an array of matching records.

explanation.beginner:
Example: courseGroupByField([{"id":"1","module":"alpha","score":2},{"id":"2","module":"beta","score":5},{"id":"3","module":"alpha","score":4}], "module") produces {"alpha":[{"id":"1","module":"alpha","score":2},{"id":"3","module":"alpha","score":4}],"beta":[{"id":"2","module":"beta","score":5}]}. Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Compare “handles empty input”: input [[],"module"] produces {}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Tempting mistake: Reinitializing an existing group erases earlier contributions. Distinct-key counts differ from total occurrences.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty input”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
